subject: CuraHealth: residency warranty, erase evidence & assisted-wipe playbook
thread_body:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@curahealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Residency warranty and erase evidence for Private VPC

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As part of our legal/regulatory review we need two things documented for the Private VPC deployment: a written residency warranty stating where customer-controlled storage resides and the mechanism and timeline for evidence of deletion after termination (both assisted and customer-initiated).

Can you share the field-evidence types you can produce (logs, snapshot tombstones, chain-of-custody artifacts), how long those artifacts are retained, and whether we can receive a signed attestation? Also interested in a short playbook for an assisted wipe (steps, expected windows, who does what).

Best,
Tom
---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@curahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 11:08:23 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency warranty and erase evidence for Private VPC

Hi Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. High level answers first, then I attached a short playbook and an evidence template for you to review. See attachments: redwood-assisted-erase-playbook-v1.pdf and erase-evidence-template.xlsx.

1) Residency warranty: For Private/VPC deployments we provide a written warranty specifying the physical region(s) (cloud provider regions or customer data center) where customer-controlled object and block storage will be located. The warranty is backed by our deployment configuration (region pins) and audit logs recorded at provisioning and snapshot times.

2) Evidence of deletion: We can provide the following artifact types after a wipe or contract termination:
  - Snapshot tombstone records (snapshot id, deletion timestamp, operator id)
  - Storage-level purge logs (object ids, purge-job id, start/end timestamps)
  - KMS key-rotation and key-deactivation timestamps (if platform-managed keys are used) or customer KMS revocation confirmation (if using customer-managed keys)
  - Access audit log extracts showing last access and purge operations
  - A signed attestation letter (standard template) confirming the steps performed and artifacts produced

Retention and windows: we retain operational logs for 90 days by default in the handback audit bucket; we can extend retention (e.g., 1 year) as a contract addendum. Evidence generation and delivery timeline for an assisted wipe is typically 3–10 business days depending on size and whether legal notarization is requested.

3) Chain of custody: For assisted operations we maintain a job record that includes the operator, source host (ID), command run, and the verification checks. If CuraHealth requires notarized handback, we can coordinate with our compliance team and provide timeboxed windows for witness/testifier presence.

Next steps: Marissa will outline the assisted-wipe runbook and Karthik will provide the technical artifacts we can export and their formats. Once you confirm the level of attestation (signed vs notarized) we can provide a firm delivery ETA.

Best,
Naomi

Naomi — quick operational clarifications from procurement/regulatory: 1) Is the attestation a standard PDF we sign, or do you issue a company-signed letterhead document? 2) If we request 12 months of audit artifact retention that's an addendum cost — can you give a ballpark? 3) We need the playbook to include an expected maximum outage window for an assisted wipe.

Thanks,
CuraHealth Procurement

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: procurement@curahealth.com; Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@curahealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency warranty and erase evidence for Private VPC

Hi —

Answers inline to keep this short: 1) Attestation format: we can produce a company-signed letter on Redwood letterhead by default. If you require notarization we will route to Legal & Compliance and add the required signing steps (adds ~5 business days).

2) Retention cost estimate: 12 months of additional evidence retention (export/cold-store of audit artifacts) is typically priced as a fixed monthly add-on. Ballpark for a mid-sized deployment is $1,200–$2,400/mo depending on total stored artifact volume and encryption storage class; we will provide a formal quote once you share estimated log volume.

3) Assisted-wipe outage window: the typical timeline in our playbook is:
  - Preparation and snapshot: 0–4 hours (can be done live)
  - Purge job execution: variable, normally 1–48 hours depending on dataset size and parallelism settings
  - Verification and evidence package prep: 1–5 business days
  - Total guaranteed SLO for assisted-wipe + evidence delivery (standard): 10 business days; expedited options available for an extra fee.

Karthik — can you upload the example CSV export format and a sample snapshot tombstone record to the shared Drive folder Naomi referenced?

Thanks,
Marissa

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>; Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>; procurement@curahealth.com
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency warranty and erase evidence for Private VPC

Uploading now to the Drive link Naomi included. Quick technical notes to complement the playbook:

- Snapshot tombstone format: {snapshot_id},{object_count},{deleted_by},{deleted_at_iso},{job_id}
- Purge logs include per-object hashes (sha256 truncated), storage node id, and purge-job id. We do not include plaintext customer data in evidence artifacts.
- KMS: if CuraHealth uses customer-managed keys (CMK), you can rotate/deactivate or revoke access immediately; we will include the CMK revocation confirmation in the evidence package.
- For chain-of-custody, we add a signed job manifest (HMAC) produced by our operations runbook that correlates job_id -> operator -> verification checks.

I can also provide a sample notarized attestation template if you decide to go that route.

Karthik
